records.title: Onboard Charger and EVSE Communication Failures
records.description: The ELR, based on the Chevrolet Volt platform, experiences onboard charger failures and communication issues with Level 2 EVSEs. The charging module may fail to initiate charging, stop mid-charge, or throw fault codes. The 120V Level 1 EVSE included with the car is also known to have reliability issues.
records.solution: Have the dealer diagnose the specific fault code. The onboard charger module may need replacement. Try different EVSEs to rule out charging station issues. Update the vehicle software to the latest calibration. The Voltec warranty may cover charging system components for 8 years/100,000 miles.
symptoms: Vehicle fails to start charging
Charging stops mid-session
Charge fault message on dash
Amber charging light instead of green
Unable to charge on specific EVSEs

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain Preventing System Boot
records.description: The 12V auxiliary battery is prone to parasitic drain, especially when the vehicle is left unplugged for extended periods. Unlike a conventional car, the ELR cannot start if the 12V battery is dead even if the main traction battery is fully charged. The vehicle's electronics draw from the 12V system even when off.
records.solution: Replace the 12V battery with a quality AGM battery — the original battery often fails within 3-4 years. Keep the vehicle plugged in when parked for extended periods, as the Voltec system maintains the 12V battery when plugged in. A battery tender connected to the 12V battery is recommended for long-term storage.
symptoms: Vehicle will not enter Ready mode
No dashboard lights
Key fob not detected
Shift to Park warning despite being in Park

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Capacity Degradation and Reduced EV Range
records.description: The Cadillac ELR (based on the Chevrolet Volt platform) uses a 16.5 kWh lithium-ion battery pack rated for 37 miles of EV range. Owners report noticeable capacity degradation after 5-7 years, with usable EV range dropping to 25-30 miles. The battery management system restricts capacity as cells degrade. While GM's Voltec system is generally more reliable than pure EV batteries due to active thermal management, the ELR's limited production means replacement battery modules are scarce and expensive.
records.solution: Battery capacity loss is gradual and the vehicle remains fully functional with the range-extending gasoline engine. GM warranty covers the battery for 8 years/100,000 miles. If battery modules need replacement, a Voltec-certified shop can replace individual cell groups rather than the entire pack. Maintaining the battery between 20-80% charge and avoiding extreme heat exposure slows degradation.
symptoms: EV range significantly lower than original 37 miles
Battery capacity bars showing fewer segments than when new
Gasoline engine engaging sooner than expected
Charging completes faster than before (less capacity to fill)
Reduced regenerative braking energy recovery

records.title: Charge Port Door Actuator Failure and Charging Issues
records.description: The ELR's motorized charge port door frequently fails to open or close properly. The electric actuator motor that operates the charge port door jams or the pivot hinge corrodes, preventing the door from releasing. In cold weather the door can freeze shut. If the door won't open, the vehicle cannot be plugged in for charging. The charge port light ring may also fail to illuminate or show incorrect colors.
records.solution: Replace the charge port door actuator assembly (GM 22828424). If the door is frozen, gentle warming with a hair dryer (not heat gun) can free it. Lubricate the hinge and latch mechanism with silicone spray every 6 months as preventive maintenance. The LED light ring module can be replaced separately.
symptoms: Charge port door does not release when pressed
Charge port door opens but won't close flush
Clicking noise from charge port area but door stays locked
Charge port LED ring not illuminating
Door freezes shut in cold weather

records.title: CUE Infotainment Touchscreen Delamination and Unresponsive Touch
records.description: The Cadillac CUE infotainment touchscreen shared across 2013-2020 Cadillacs (including the ELR) suffers from a well-documented delamination failure. The capacitive touch film separates from the glass, creating air bubbles, spider-web cracks radiating from the lower bezel, ghost touches, lag, and eventually a screen that will not respond to input at all. Because nearly every climate, audio, navigation and EV/charge-setting function on the ELR routes through CUE, a failed screen cripples a large share of the car's controls. The defect was widespread enough to trigger a class-action lawsuit (Cadillac CUE delamination) alleging a flaw in the sensing-panel production or screen installation. Failures commonly appear after the car has seen heat cycling, often well past the basic warranty.
records.solution: Most owners avoid the ~$1,200-$1,500 dealer replacement of the entire faceplate/radio assembly by installing just the touch-sensor/LCD panel. Common OEM CUE display part numbers referenced for these cars are 23243166, 22980207, 22980208, 22986276, 22935061, 20867045 and 22912608 (verify the variant - with vs. without heated/cooled-seat function - against your VIN before ordering, as the wrong configuration will not enable all buttons). Gel-free aftermarket replacement panels (e.g., from CUE-screen specialists) run roughly $150-$300 and reuse the existing electronics; mail-in board/screen refurb services are a lower-cost alternative. Replacement is a known DIY-friendly job (remove trim bezel, swap panel, transfer ribbon cables).
symptoms: Bubbling or delamination starting at the bottom edge of the screen
Spider-web cracks spreading across the display without impact
Touchscreen unresponsive or registering phantom/ghost touches
Laggy or frozen interface, random resets
Loss of access to climate, audio, navigation and charge settings

records.title: Electronic Stability Control Diagnostic Software Defect (NHTSA Recall 14V144000) - No Warning When ESC Is Disabled
records.description: GM recalled 656 model year 2014 Cadillac ELR vehicles not equipped with adaptive cruise control (built September 26, 2013 through February 14, 2014) because the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) software could block certain ESC self-diagnostics. As a result, if the electronic stability control system became partially or fully disabled, the software might not illuminate the warning telltale to alert the driver, so the driver could continue operating the car believing stability control was active when it was not, increasing the risk of loss of directional control. This is an EBCM software/diagnostic-logic defect, separate from any ABS wheel-speed hardware or brake-hydraulic issue.
records.solution: Under NHTSA recall 14V144000, dealers recalibrate/reprogram the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) with corrected ESC diagnostic software, free of charge. Owners should confirm completion by VIN; the remedy is a software flash and requires no parts. The recall began April 17, 2014.
symptoms: Stability control (StabiliTrak) may be disabled without any dashboard warning light
Loss of expected traction/stability intervention with no driver notification
Potential loss of directional control in slippery or evasive maneuvers

records.title: Engine Forced to Run by Fuel/Engine Maintenance Mode After Sitting Unused
records.description: Because many ELRs are driven mostly on electricity and sit for long periods, owners frequently panic when the gas engine forces itself on and will not stay off - thinking the car is broken. This is actually two by-design protection routines. Fuel Maintenance Mode (FMM) runs the engine to burn off fuel once the tank's average fuel age exceeds ~1 year, and will not release grid/Hold mode until fresh fuel is added. Engine Maintenance Mode (EMM) runs the engine after roughly six weeks of little/no engine operation to circulate oil and keep seals conditioned. Both display a brief notice on the CUE screen at startup. The high search demand is from owners mistaking normal maintenance behavior for a fault, and from stale-fuel driveability problems in cars that sit.
records.solution: Confirm the on-screen FMM/EMM message - this is normal operation, not a defect, and the routine cannot be aborted mid-cycle. For FMM, add several gallons of fresh fuel to lower the tank's average fuel age, which lets the car return to normal EV/Hold operation; for EMM, simply let the engine complete its short run cycle. To prevent it: drive the car on engine power occasionally, keep at least a quarter tank of fresh fuel, and use the tank periodically. If the engine runs rough or throws codes after long storage, treat it as stale-fuel driveability (fresh fuel, possibly fuel system cleaning) rather than an internal engine fault.
symptoms: Gas engine starts and stays running with battery charge available
'Fuel Maintenance Mode' or 'Engine Maintenance Mode' message at startup
Hold mode unavailable until fresh fuel is added
Engine runs after the car has sat for weeks/months
Rough running on old fuel after long storage

records.title: Front Seat Hook Bracket Weld Defect (NHTSA Recall 14V446000) - Seat May Not Stay Secured in a Crash
records.description: GM recalled 2014 Cadillac ELR vehicles as part of a broader recall (covering 2013-2014 Buick Encore and Cadillac ATS; 2014 Cadillac CTS, ELR, Chevrolet Caprice and SS; and 2014-2015 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra) for an incomplete weld on the front-seat hook bracket assembly of the lower seat track. Because the bracket is not fully welded, the front seat may not remain secured to the floor during a high-load event such as a crash, increasing the risk of occupant injury. This is a manufacturing/structural safety defect the owner cannot detect by feel during normal use; the recall remedy is inspection of the weld. GM's number for this recall is 14340; the remedy began August 15, 2014.
records.solution: Under NHTSA recall 14V446000, Cadillac dealers inspect the seat hook bracket assembly weld and replace the lower seat track as necessary, free of charge. Owners should verify by VIN that the recall has been completed and, if not, schedule the free inspection/repair at a Cadillac dealer. There is no reliable aftermarket alternative because it is a structural weld to the seat track.
symptoms: No driver-detectable symptom during normal driving
Seat could shift or detach from the floor track under crash loads
Possible seat looseness on the track in severe cases

records.title: Gas Engine Engages Prematurely Before EV Range Is Used Up
records.description: A heavily discussed ELR complaint (the single largest forum thread for the car) is the range-extender gas engine firing up while the battery gauge still shows charge remaining, or switching to engine power 'too soon' after a fresh charge. As cells age and fall out of balance, the control system starts the engine early to keep the weakest cell from dropping into a damaging low-voltage state and to supplement propulsion. Owners report the engine running far more than expected and the all-electric portion shrinking unpredictably. This is distinct from simple range fade - the user-facing symptom is unexpected engine engagement and erratic EV-to-engine transitions.
records.solution: Rule out the benign causes first: cold ambient temperatures, a hot or cold HV battery, an unlatched hood, or an active Engine/Fuel Maintenance Mode all legitimately start the engine with charge remaining. If none apply, have a Voltec-certified dealer read the HV pack's cell-balance and state-of-health data; an unbalanced pack can sometimes be improved with a balancing/charge routine, but a genuinely degraded pack requires module or full battery replacement (covered under the 8-year/100,000-mile, or California 10-year/150,000-mile, HV warranty if within limits). Keeping the car regularly charged and avoiding leaving it at very low/high state of charge helps slow imbalance.
symptoms: Engine starts while battery gauge still shows charge
EV-only range shorter and shrinking year over year
Frequent or early switching from electric to engine power
Engine runs more than expected in mild conditions
Final battery bars deplete much faster than the rest

records.title: Loss of Propulsion / 'Propulsion Power Reduced' from Low HV Battery Cell Voltage
records.description: The ELR's 16.5/17.1 kWh Voltec battery can gradually lose the ability to maintain cell voltage, and as cells age and fall out of balance the car can throw a 'PROPULSION POWER REDUCED' message (often with a check-engine light), refuse to charge, drop into a limp/reduced-propulsion mode, or fail to start. GM issued a recall (covering 2014-2016 ELR and 2012-2015 Volt) for this condition. Owners report range collapsing and, in worse cases, the powertrain derating while driving - a safety concern. This is the cell-voltage/propulsion-loss failure mode specifically, distinct from normal range fade.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform the recall: GM reprograms the Hybrid Powertrain Control Module 2 (HPCM2) to give earlier warning of a weakening pack (this software was free under the recall through 6/30/2021; confirm VIN status with Cadillac/NHTSA). Note the reflash only improves the warning - it does NOT restore capacity. If the pack itself has weak/unbalanced cells, the genuine fix is a battery module or full HV pack replacement; the high-voltage components are covered under the 8-year/100,000-mile Voltec warranty (10-year/150,000-mile in California AT-PZEV states). Have a Voltec-certified dealer scan and report cell-balance/state-of-health data before quoting a pack.
symptoms: 'Propulsion Power Reduced' message on the driver display
Check-engine light with charging disabled
Sudden reduced power / limp mode while driving
Vehicle will not start or will not charge
Sharp drop in usable EV range

records.title: Brake Rotor Corrosion and Pulsation from Infrequent Use
records.description: The ELR's regenerative braking system means the friction brakes are used very infrequently, especially in city driving. This causes the brake rotors to develop surface rust and corrosion that is not worn away by normal pad contact. The corroded rotors create pulsation, vibration, and reduced braking effectiveness. Brake pads can also seize in the caliper brackets from lack of use. This is a common issue across all plug-in hybrid and EV vehicles but is exacerbated on the ELR due to its aggressive regen-on-demand paddle.
records.solution: Perform monthly highway-speed brake applications to clean rotor surfaces — 3-4 firm stops from 60 mph. Have brake pads removed, cleaned, and re-lubricated with ceramic brake grease at every tire rotation. If rotors are pitted from corrosion, they must be resurfaced or replaced. Use coated or ceramic-coated replacement rotors for better corrosion resistance.
symptoms: Brake pedal pulsation when stopping
Scraping or grinding noise on first few brake applications
Visible orange rust buildup on brake rotors
Reduced braking effectiveness
Steering wheel vibration during braking

records.title: 'Service High Voltage Charging System' Message from Low Battery Coolant or Failed Coolant Level Sensor
records.description: The ELR uses a dedicated liquid loop to thermally manage the high-voltage battery, with a coolant level sensor in the HV battery reservoir on the driver's side of the engine bay. A low coolant level - or, very commonly, a failing coolant level sensor or its jumper harness with internal wire breaks - triggers a 'Service High Voltage Charging System' (SHVCS) message, often setting P3000 and disabling charging. This is a well-known Voltec failure that has migrated from the Chevy Volt to the higher-mileage ELR fleet. Left unaddressed it can interrupt charging and, in conjunction with thermal-management faults, contribute to reduced-propulsion behavior.
records.solution: First check the HV battery coolant reservoir (driver's side) and top off to the top of the black label - GM's fill spec was revised upward to prevent nuisance messages; use the correct GM HV battery coolant (GM P/N 12378390, a dedicated 50/50 low-conductivity DexCool-type fluid - do NOT substitute ordinary coolant in the HV loop). If level is fine or the message returns, replace the drive-motor battery coolant level sensor (GM P/N 22922224) and inspect/replace the sensor jumper harness (P/N 13586114), a known intermittent-failure point. Scan and clear P3000 after repair. HV-system repairs fall under the 8-year/100,000-mile Voltec warranty.
symptoms: 'Service High Voltage Charging System' message
Vehicle will not charge or charging is interrupted
P3000 high-voltage system fault stored
Check-engine light
Low coolant in the HV battery reservoir

records.title: "Shift to Park" False Warning from Failing Electronic Shifter Park Switch
records.description: The ELR uses an electronic precision shift lever that springs back to a center rest position and relies on an internal park-detent microswitch to confirm the transmission is in Park. On the ELR this internal park switch degrades and intermittently fails to send the 'in Park' signal, producing a persistent 'Shift to Park' warning even though the lever is already in Park, which prevents the driver from powering the car down. The fault is intermittent (can occur several times a day, then disappear for a week), which is characteristic of a worn switch contact rather than a software glitch. When it occurs, the car may repeatedly chime and stay awake until it times out (owners report roughly 20 minutes), and repeated occurrences can contribute to 12V battery drain. Owners on the Cadillac and GM-Volt forums document the identical symptom, and the same GM electronic-shifter 'Shift to Park' condition became the subject of a nationwide class-action lawsuit.
records.solution: Temporary workaround owners report: lightly pull the lever out of the Park detent and release, or flick the small silver override switch on the back of the shifter, which forces the car into shutdown. The accepted permanent repair is replacement of the electronic precision shift lever/console shifter assembly; owners report the part costs over $200 and total dealer repair around $548. If the shifter left systems awake and drained the 12V battery, it may need recharging or replacement at the same time.
symptoms: 'Shift to Park' message displayed even though the lever is in Park

records.title: Sudden Total Loss of Electrical Power While Driving (Often With No Stored Codes)
records.description: Multiple ELR owners report a frightening intermittent failure in which the car loses ALL electrical power without warning while driving - sometimes preceded by a loud 'pop' - taking out power steering, power brake assist, lights, hazard flashers, gauges and even door locks, forcing the driver to wrestle the car to the shoulder. A defining (and maddening) trait is that the car frequently restarts normally after towing and leaves no diagnostic trouble codes, so dealers struggle to reproduce or diagnose it. Suspected sources include the 12V system/grounds, the high-voltage contactor/relay in the battery, or the battery energy control module, but root cause is often not confirmed.
records.solution: Treat as a safety-priority intermittent electrical fault. Start with a thorough 12V battery, charging and ground-circuit inspection (a weak or marginal 12V auxiliary system is a common trigger on Voltec cars), then have a Voltec-certified tech inspect the HV battery disconnect/contactors and high-current connections for arcing or loose terminals (consistent with the reported 'pop'). Capture freeze-frame/history data immediately after an event before clearing anything, and document each occurrence for GM, since the lack of stored codes makes a contemporaneous log the best diagnostic lever. Costs range from a cheap ground/terminal repair to HV contactor or module replacement.
symptoms: Complete electrical shutdown while driving
Loud 'pop' before power loss in some cases
Loss of power steering and power brake assist
Dash, lights, flashers and door locks all dead
Car restarts normally later with no fault codes
